themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Most of these problems have no answer key, and the thing being measured often changes while you measure it. So the models start small: build a handful of cases they can actually prove, then grade everything else against that.
themes.evidence: Identity resolution answers call accuracy claims unfalsifiable without a consenting panel, answer engine work has no stable baseline because models drift between runs, incrementality answers say the platform re-optimizes against the holdout, and today's journey orchestration answers ask for a person-level holdout and one honest contact log before anything is blocked.

themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls are about meaning and worth, not data: whether a picture plus a headline implies a promise, whether evidence really backs a claim, what the word customer means, what a message is worth. No formula settles these, because the disagreement usually has budget attached.
themes.evidence: Content governance answers say an implied claim emerges from combinations no checker sees, semantic layer answers call conflicting definitions of customer a political settlement rather than a modeling gap, and today's journey orchestration answers all say nobody can agree what better means across conversion, fatigue, service and lifetime value.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what happens next, they build one door they own and push everything through it. A sent email or a spent dollar cannot be called back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: Agent execution answers converge on a proxy or gateway with hard spend, rate and audience caps because sends and spend have no rollback, downstream consent answers route every data exit through a single checkpoint, and today's journey orchestration answers propose one central switch or shared ledger that every channel must check before sending.

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, a dollar, or a message leaves your own systems, you cannot look inside the partner, ad platform, or trained model that now holds it. The best anyone offers is watching from the outside: expiring lists, planted test records, and hoping behavior matches the promise.
themes.evidence: Consent enforcement answers say you cannot read back a third party's deletion and cannot untrain one person's influence without rebuilding the model, agent execution answers note vendors expose no staging or undo primitives, and ad supply answers say the parties measuring the traffic often profit from it.

themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Many of these problems stall because the party holding the answer gains nothing by handing it over, and nobody can force them. So the models either try to make honesty pay better than hiding, or they stop waiting for cooperation and work only with what they already own.
themes.evidence: Agentic traffic answers build a fast declared-agent lane so declaring beats spoofing, identity answers say platform owners profit from broken cross-device links, and today's journey orchestration answers say channel leaders will subvert central coordination because their bonuses reward local volume.
